survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is based on questionnaires administered to ECEC staff and setting leaders, with the aim of producing representative samples within each participating country/subnational entity for each ECEC level. The note reports indicator percentages and percentage-point differences derived from the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database; however, this participant note does not specify the exact complex survey weighting variables or replicate-weight procedures used in the computations. The report cautions that low response rates can create non-response bias and that estimates should be interpreted with caution for systems annotated with response-rate technical issues. For analysts using the underlying database, the appropriate approach is to apply the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 complex survey design weights provided with the database (and any replicate weights if supplied) when estimating population-representative percentages for staff and leaders.

As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported indicators. The note also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure for questionnaire responses, so missing-data handling is not reported; this is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, though it does not affect the fact that the outputs are descriptive survey indicators.

It states that TALIS Starting Strong 2024 uses representative samples of staff and leaders within each participating country/subnational entity for each ECEC level, and it annotates systems that did not meet technical standards with respect to response rates (pre-primary ISCED 02: Germany, Ireland, Norway; under age 3: Flemish Community of Belgium, Ireland, New Brunswick, Norway, Quebec). No further student-level inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific questionnaire item completion thresholds or analytic-sample sizes) are provided in the participant note.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD participant note summarizes descriptive results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024, a large-scale survey of early childhood education and care (ECEC) staff and setting leaders. The note reports indicator percentages based on self-reports about staff time use, training coverage, professional development needs, family engagement practices, leader–staff feedback and collaboration, workforce retention-related stressors, and governance/management characteristics. Data collection occurred first in 2018 and was extended in 2024 to additional countries and subnational entities, including 15 at pre-primary (ISCED level 02) and 8 for settings serving children under age 3. The note focuses on New Brunswick and Quebec (Canada) for children under age 3 and compares them with other participating systems. Estimates are presented with caution because low response rates can introduce non-response bias, and some systems are annotated for not meeting response-rate technical standards; the note does not provide model-based performance metrics or ML-based causal claims.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD results note rather than an empirical ML study: it does not train or evaluate predictive models, does not report plausible values, and does not provide an analytic-sample size at the student level. Consequently, fields such as total_students, per-country n_students, and ML technique lists are not available from the provided text. The extraction therefore focuses on survey scope, indicator sources, and the reported descriptive comparisons for New Brunswick and Quebec.
